answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The opal multiplier is published, charged in glacier, and umber lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2164 identities would post 2984 proofs and burn roughly 31 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
